```json
{
  "winner": "B",
  "reasons": [
    "B has direct evidence that buyers pay. Several competitors publish live pricing: Expiration Reminder at $49-$349/mo, RenewalTracker at $49/mo, and ClearBot at $500-$800 per location per year. In A, the priced entrants are thin. Nalvis is pre-launch and waitlist-only, mendapi's hosted tier has no price, Since.dev's Pro price is undisclosed, and only Since.dev's $149/mo Studio tier is disclosed and presented as live.",
    "A's brief itself notes that several competitors are open-sourcing their core detection engines for free. That puts structural downward pressure on A's price anchor. B's comparables show a stable paid tier at $29-$99/mo that a lean MVP can match.",
    "A's trust barrier looks like a harder blocker inside 90 days. A must get write access to customers' production code to open PRs, and its own brief says SOC 2 Type II is commonly expected and likely out of scope. B's baseline MVP (deadline tracking, alerts, AI parsing of renewal notices) can run on dates the customer enters, with a lower security bar.",
    "B's demand quotes come from practitioners describing their own manual workarounds, across three separate occupational communities. Some of A's demand evidence comes from posts by people who built and are promoting their own fixes, which is weaker as a signal of buyer demand.",
    "B can avoid its riskiest piece, 50-state rule-change monitoring, by launching as a narrow vertical tracker. A cannot avoid its core risk, repo access, because opening PRs is the product.",
    "A does have cheaper acquisition channels (GitHub Marketplace, dev.to) than B's paid search at $87-$200 per lead. However, B's CPL figure is flagged as directional, and a single paying customer in 90 days can plausibly come from Reddit and community outreach."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "A's price hypothesis is anchored partly on Nalvis's '$14/mo hosted tier', but Nalvis is pre-launch and waitlist-only, so that price shows no revenue or willingness to pay. The other anchor, Since.dev's $149/mo Studio tier, is the only disclosed price that appears live, and neither brief gives any evidence of actual paying customers for it.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate-to-low confidence. Both briefs describe saturated markets with 7-15 competitors. Both show real pain where many users currently rely on DIY workarounds (spreadsheets, homegrown fixes). B wins mainly because its competitors' published pricing shows buyers already pay, and because it faces a lower trust and compliance hurdle to a first sale. Neither brief shows a clear wedge for a new solo entrant."
}
```
